questions.correct_answer: If a language is regular, then it can be pumped.
questions.explanation: The Pumping Lemma states that if a language is regular, then any string in the language of sufficient length can be divided into three parts that can be 'pumped' to create new strings that are also in the language. The converse is not true; a language that can be pumped is not necessarily regular.
options: If a language is infinite, then it can be pumped.
If a language is regular, then it can be pumped.
If a language can be pumped, then it is regular.
If a language is not regular, then it cannot be pumped.

L is undecidable because it is not regular.

L is undecidable because no algorithm can determine if a string is in L.
